subject: GoodHealth — audit readiness & recommended hosting route (post-demo)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ara Singh <ara@ghanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & ask: hosting route implications for PHI / next evidence items

Hi Ara — thanks again for the demo call today. Quick recap and proposed asks so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- GoodHealth will be ingesting PHI (clinical notes + structured claims) for the initial pilot (~3k patients).
- Primary goal: low-latency clinical summarization for clinician workflows (latency target <300ms).
- Procurement & security teams will require a signed BAA and SOC 2 evidence pack before production.

Redwood options we discussed (tradeoffs)
- Hosted API (fast onboarding): lowest time-to-value, but would require GoodHealth to accept Redwood managed environment + BAA; may not satisfy air-gap requirements.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs): provides tenant isolation and better SLA/latency; can be paired with VPC peering and strict network controls.
- Private VPC / On-prem (full isolation): best for compliance/audit posture but adds deployment time and managed support overhead.

Requested items from GoodHealth (helpful to qualify routing decision)
1) Confirm whether PHI will be stored at rest in requests/responses or only transiently processed.
2) Procurement target signing date for BAA (procurement@goodhealth.com).
3) Are there mandatory auditors (external firm) that need direct evidence uploads?
4) Any internal policy requiring on-prem (air-gapped) deployments?

Attachments: BAA template and SOC2 evidence checklist attached for your review.

Next suggested step
- If procurement can sign BAA within 2 weeks and PHI is transient, recommend Dedicated capacity with VPC peering (best balance of latency + compliance).
- If procurement requires on-prem or full private control plane, we should identify timeline (4–8 weeks) and scope.

Can you confirm the answers to (1)-(4) and propose two 30-min time slots for a short security sync with your CS & procurement folks?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internal owners once I have the times.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
v: 415-555-0198

Attachments:
- Redwood_BAA_template_v1.2.pdf (pdf)
- SOC2-evidence-summary.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ara Singh <ara@ghanalytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@goodhealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & ask: hosting route implications for PHI / next evidence items

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and clarifications: 

1) PHI handling: we need to retain certain fields for 30 days for auditability (so not purely transient). That pushes us toward dedicated/private choices.
2) Procurement: they want to see a BAA first, then legal will review pricing/terms. They can target sign-off in ~3 weeks if the BAA is standard.
3) Auditors: our external auditor is "Clearway Audit" — they will request scoped SOC2 artifacts. They will likely expect direct evidence uploads to a shared drive.
4) Air-gap: not a hard requirement today, but the security team prefers customer-controlled network isolation (VPC or private control plane).

On hosting preference: the dev team prefers Dedicated for performance; security would prefer Private or Dedicated + strict VPC controls. Can you confirm what evidence Redwood can provide to Clearway and approximate timeline for evidence delivery?

I can do a quick sync with procurement + security on Thu 26 Aug 10:00-10:30 PT or Fri 27 Aug 11:00-11:30 PT. Which works for you?

—Ara
Ara Singh
CTO, GoodHealth Analytics
ara@ghanalytics.com

Subject: Re: Recap & ask: hosting route implications for PHI / next evidence items

Thanks Vanessa / Ara — jumping in with technical fit + evidence timeline from our side. 

Evidence we can provide to Clearway Audit
- SOC 2 (Type II) report: we can provide the latest certified report and scoped narratives (available within 2 business days for review).
- Controls evidence: we can produce logs, change-control documents, and configuration snapshots for the hosting layer (scope permitting) within 5 business days.
- Network diagrams and VPC peering plan: draft within 2 business days; final after peering test.

Recommended hosting configuration (based on your inputs)
- Pilot (recommended): Dedicated capacity with private VPC peering + strict egress rules. This gives: low latency (<300ms median) and a clear evidence path for auditors.
- If procurement insists on customer-controlled control plane: Redwood Private (VPC + private control plane) — expected ramp 4–8 weeks, additional ops support included.

Operational notes
- For the Dedicated + VPC option we will: provide a scoped SOC2 evidence bundle, execute a BAA (DocuSign link to be sent), and schedule a short peer-connection dry run before pilot start.
- On retention: we support configurable request logging; if GoodHealth requires 30-day retention of certain PHI fields, we can enable field-level retention controls and provide the retention policy artifact.

Attachments: deployment-options-matrix.csv (matrix comparing Hosted / Dedicated / Private with timelines & evidence items).

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Procurement reviews attached BAA template; sign or mark redlines (target: 3 weeks).
2) GoodHealth confirms required retention scope (fields + duration) so we can finalize evidence plan.
3) Book 30-min security sync on Thu 26 Aug 10:00 PT (Vanessa, I added that slot as Ara proposed).

Happy to jump on the call and walk through the evidence list.

—Rishi
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachments:

If this sounds good I’ll lock the timeline and route the internal engineering onboarding tasks. Appreciate the quick turnaround — this keeps us on track for a Sept pilot.
